teaser.text: ConocoPhillips finds oil and gas, brings them out of the ground and sells them to businesses that turn them into energy and materials. Its business is therefore a chain of products, prices, costs and deliveries, not a retail fuel brand.

blocks.heading: What has to go right or wrong for ConocoPhillips?

paragraphs.text: EBITDA is the main operating assumption. The base case rises from $30,061 million in October 2027 to $34,007 million in October 2029; the table shows the intermediate year. The bear case falls from $22,685 million to $22,283 million, while the bull case rises from $36,299 million to $43,280 million. The base starts near the $30,340 million margin proxy derived from 2025 production, prices and costs. The company also guides to production of 2.295–2.325 million BOE per day and expects project income and lower spending to improve cash flow. The bear reflects the 4% acquisition-adjusted production decline reported in 2026 Q2 and Qatar disruption.

The bull case leads from $223.17 to $335.41. Qatar recovers promptly, Willow and LNG start near schedule, construction spending eases and strong cash flow funds both investment and shareholder returns. Its 15% probability reflects the need for several uncertain events to succeed together, including project timing and cost control.

blocks.heading: How much does ConocoPhillips pay its shareholders?

paragraphs.text: Dividend growth is measured in the base case, from $3.36 per share in October 2027 to $3.64 in October 2029. The bear holds at $2.80, while the bull reaches $4.00. The base begins with the current $0.84 quarterly dividend, and the five-year record shows annual DPS rising to $3.18 in 2025. The bear allows for a cut because commodity cash flow is cyclical; COP reduced its dividend sharply in 2016. The bull requires project cash to arrive as planned.

earnings.opening: ConocoPhillips reports its next results on November 5, 2026. The key watch is how much cash remained after spending.
earnings.closing: The full memo answers what ConocoPhillips does, how it compares with rivals, who runs it, and what risks could change its path.

paragraphs.text: For 2026, management guides to production of 2.295–2.325 million barrels of oil equivalent per day and capital spending of $12.0–$12.5 billion. A barrel of oil equivalent, or BOE, converts oil and natural gas into one energy measure; it is not necessarily a barrel of oil earning the oil price. Production and spending are separate promises.

blocks.heading: Has ConocoPhillips kept its past promises?

paragraphs.text: The buyback promise is less comfortable. COP expected more than US$7 billion of repurchases in the first full year after the acquisition, subject to commodity prices, but actual repurchases fell short. COP nevertheless reported returning 45% of defined cash from operations to shareholders in 2025.

blocks.heading: What is ConocoPhillips's revenue and profit trend?

paragraphs.text: Revenue rose from $14,740 million to $19,522 million. Net income nearly doubled, even though production fell from 2,391 to 2,248 thousand BOE a day. This is the clearest recent reminder that a producer can earn more while extracting less.

blocks.heading: What should I watch in ConocoPhillips's next results?

paragraphs.text: On November 5, 2026, COP reports third-quarter results. The report should show whether Qatar’s expected ramp occurred, whether production met guidance and how much cash remained after spending. Existing LNG recovery will not prove that construction at North Field East and South has recovered every lost week.
